title: 1.3 EXPLORATION AND PRODUCTION
summary:
Deepwater drilling activity as an oil-price sentiment indicator, Mineral rights ownership and licensing for E&P: Energy companies lease land to extract fuel and compensate both the surface land owner and the mineral rights owner (often the same or different parties) via ro

This chapter surveys how fossil fuels are located and brought out of the ground, framing exploration and production as separate specialized activities. It covers the physical side — how hydrocarbons form, migrate, and become trapped in reservoirs, how carbon chain length and gas-oil ratios classify what's produced, and how different techniques (traditional wells, fracking, shale processing, oil sands extraction, deepwater drilling) suit different rock and fuel types — alongside the business and legal side, including mineral rights leasing, the landman role, service and production sharing contract structures, reserve classification, and common unit conversions like BOE/TOE. Deepwater drilling and fracking are also noted for their broader implications, serving respectively as a price sentiment signal and a source of environmental tradeoffs.
